source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Preserves sequence, companions, crossing, named ravine, garden, and shared entry.
verses.before: After Jesus said these things, he went out with his disciples across the Kidron valley, where there was a garden. He and his disciples entered it.
verses.after: After saying these things, Jesus went out with his disciples across the Kidron ravine, where there was a garden. He and his disciples entered it.
verses.tsw_comparator: After Jesus had spoken these words, he went out with his disciples across the Kidron Valley, where there was a garden, which he and his disciples entered.

verses.rationale: Keeps Judas’s role, knowledge, and reason.
verses.before: Judas, the one handing him over, also knew the place because Jesus often met there with his disciples.
verses.after: Judas, who was betraying him, also knew the place, because Jesus had often gathered there with his disciples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Judas, who betrayed him, also knew the place, because Jesus often met there with his disciples.

verses.rationale: Preserves the armed group, its sponsors, lights, and weapons.
verses.before: So Judas took a cohort of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees and came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
verses.after: So Judas brought a cohort of soldiers and officers from the chief priests and Pharisees, and came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Judas brought a cohort of soldiers and some officers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, and they came there with lanterns and torches and weapons.

verses.rationale: Keeps Jesus’ knowledge, initiative, movement, and question.
verses.before: Jesus, knowing everything that was about to happen to him, went out and asked them, “Who are you looking for?”
verses.after: Jesus, knowing everything that was about to happen to him, stepped forward and asked them, “Whom are you looking for?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jesus, knowing all that would happen to him, came forward and said to them, “Whom are you looking for?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the identification, absolute wording’s ordinary force, and Judas’s position.
verses.before: They answered, “Jesus the Nazarene.” He said, “I am.” Judas, the one handing him over, was standing with them.
verses.after: They answered him, “Jesus the Nazarene.” He told them, “I am he.” Judas, who was betraying him, was standing with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They answered him, “Jesus of Nazareth.” Jesus said to them, “I am he.” Judas, who betrayed him, was standing with them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated declaration and physical reaction.
verses.before: When Jesus said, “I am,” they drew back and fell to the ground.
verses.after: When Jesus told them, “I am he,” they drew back and fell to the ground.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Jesus said to them, “I am he,” they drew back and fell to the ground.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated question and answer.
verses.before: Again he asked, “Who are you looking for?” They said, “Jesus the Nazarene.”
verses.after: So he asked them again, “Whom are you looking for?” They answered, “Jesus the Nazarene.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So he asked them again, “Whom are you looking for?” And they said, “Jesus of Nazareth.”

verses.rationale: Keeps self-identification, condition, and protection of the disciples.
verses.before: Jesus answered, “I told you that I am. So if you are looking for me, let these people go.”
verses.after: Jesus replied, “I told you that I am he. So if you are looking for me, let these men go.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered, “I told you that I am he. So if you are looking for me, let these go.”

verses.rationale: Preserves narrator’s fulfillment connection and quotation.
verses.before: This happened so that the word he had spoken would be fulfilled: “I did not lose one of those you gave me.”
verses.after: This happened so that the word he had spoken would be fulfilled: “I did not lose one of those you gave me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: This was to fulfill the word that he had spoken: “Of those you gave me I have lost not one.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Peter, weapon, violence, body side, status, and name.
verses.before: Simon Peter had a sword. He drew it, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his right ear. The slave’s name was Malchus.
verses.after: Then Simon Peter, who had a sword, drew it and struck the high priest’s slave, cutting off his right ear. The slave’s name was Malchus.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his right ear. The slave’s name was Malchus.

verses.rationale: Preserves command, sword and sheath, cup image, Father, and rhetorical question.
verses.before: Jesus said to Peter, “Put the sword into its sheath. Should I not drink the cup the Father has given me?”
verses.after: Jesus told Peter, “Put the sword into its sheath. Should I not drink the cup the Father has given me?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus said to Peter, “Put your sword into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup that the Father has given me?”

verses.rationale: Keeps all arresting parties, seizure, and binding while identifying the officers’ leadership context.
verses.before: Then the cohort, its commander, and the Jewish officers arrested Jesus and bound him.
verses.after: Then the cohort, its commander, and the Judean leaders’ officers arrested Jesus and bound him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the soldiers, their officer, and the Judean officers arrested Jesus and bound him.

verses.rationale: Preserves first destination and family and office explanation.
verses.before: They led him first to Annas, because he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
verses.after: They took him first to Annas, because he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
verses.tsw_comparator: First they led him to Annas, for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.

verses.rationale: Keeps the retrospective identification and political counsel.
verses.before: Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jewish leaders that it was better for one man to die for the people.
verses.after: Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Judean leaders that it was better for one man to die for the people.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was Caiaphas who had advised the Judeans that it was better to have one person die for the people.

verses.rationale: Preserves both followers and the other disciple’s access and reason.
verses.before: Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. That disciple was known to the high priest and entered the high priest’s courtyard with Jesus.
verses.after: Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. That disciple was known to the high priest, so he went with Jesus into the high priest’s courtyard.
verses.tsw_comparator: Simon Peter followed Jesus, and so did another disciple. Since that disciple was known to the high priest, he entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest,

verses.rationale: Keeps Peter’s location and the access sequence; the gatekeeper is female in the next verse.
verses.before: But Peter stood outside at the door. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out, spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.
verses.after: Peter remained outside by the gate. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out, spoke to the gatekeeper, and brought Peter in.
verses.tsw_comparator: but Peter stood outside at the door. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the woman who kept the door, and brought Peter in.

verses.rationale: Preserves her role and gender, loaded question, and first denial.
verses.before: The servant girl guarding the door said to Peter, “You are not one of this man’s disciples too, are you?” He said, “I am not.”
verses.after: The servant girl who kept the gate asked Peter, “You are not one of this man’s disciples too, are you?” He answered, “I am not.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The woman who kept the door said to Peter, “You are not also one of this man’s disciples, are you?” He said, “I am not.”

verses.rationale: Keeps weather, charcoal fire, group, Peter’s location, and repetition.
verses.before: The slaves and officers had made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and they were standing around warming themselves. Peter was also standing with them, warming himself.
verses.after: The slaves and officers had made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and they were standing around warming themselves. Peter was also standing with them, warming himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the slaves and the officers were standing around a charcoal fire they had made, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves. Peter also was with them, standing and warming himself.

verses.rationale: Preserves both subjects of the interrogation.
verses.before: The high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.
verses.after: Meanwhile, the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and his teaching.
verses.tsw_comparator: The high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching.

verses.rationale: Keeps public speech, teaching locations, Jewish setting, and denial of secret doctrine.
verses.before: Jesus answered, “I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where all Jewish people gather. I said nothing in secret.
verses.after: Jesus answered him, “I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in a synagogue and in the temple courts, where all the Jewish people gather. I said nothing in secret.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered him, “I have spoken openly to the world. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where all the Judeans gather, and I have said nothing in secret.

verses.rationale: Preserves challenge, appeal to hearers, and emphatic witness.
verses.before: Why are you questioning me? Ask those who heard what I told them. Look—they know what I said.”
verses.after: Why question me? Question those who heard what I told them. Look, they know what I said.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Why do you question me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them. Look—they know what I said.”

verses.rationale: Keeps real physical abuse, officer, and accusatory question.
verses.before: When Jesus said this, one of the officers standing nearby slapped him and said, “Is that how you answer the high priest?”
verses.after: When Jesus said this, one of the officers standing nearby slapped him and said, “Is that how you answer the high priest?”
verses.tsw_comparator: When he had said this, one of the officers standing by struck Jesus with his hand, saying, “Is that how you answer the high priest?”

verses.rationale: Preserves legal challenge, contrast, and naming of violence.
verses.before: Jesus answered him, “If I spoke wrongly, testify about what was wrong. But if I spoke rightly, why do you strike me?”
verses.after: Jesus answered him, “If I spoke wrongly, testify to what was wrong. But if I spoke rightly, why do you hit me?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered him, “If I have spoken wrongly, testify about the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike me?”

verses.rationale: Keeps sender, continued restraint, and destination.
verses.before: Then Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
verses.after: Then Annas sent him, still bound, to Caiaphas the high priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Annas then sent him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.

verses.rationale: Preserves setting, repeated loaded question, explicit denial, and reply.
verses.before: Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. They asked him, “You are not one of his disciples too, are you?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
verses.after: Simon Peter was still standing and warming himself. So they asked him, “You are not one of his disciples too, are you?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. So they said to him, “You are not also one of his disciples, are you?” He denied it and said, “I am not.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the witness’s status, family connection, remembered violence, and question.
verses.before: One of the high priest’s slaves, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, “Did I not see you in the garden with him?”
verses.after: One of the high priest’s slaves—a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off—asked, “Didn’t I see you in the garden with him?”
verses.tsw_comparator: One of the slaves of the high priest, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, “Did I not see you in the garden with him?”

verses.rationale: Preserves third denial’s sequence and immediate sign.
verses.before: Peter denied it again, and immediately a rooster crowed.
verses.after: Peter denied it again, and immediately a rooster crowed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Peter again denied it; and at once a rooster crowed.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement, time, Gentile headquarters, purity concern, and Passover purpose.
verses.before: Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s headquarters. It was early morning. They themselves did not enter the headquarters so they would not become defiled but could eat the Passover.
verses.after: Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s headquarters. It was early morning. They did not enter the headquarters themselves, so that they would not become ceremonially unclean but could eat the Passover meal.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s headquarters. It was early morning. They themselves did not enter the headquarters, so that they would not be defiled, but could eat the Passover.

verses.rationale: Preserves Pilate’s movement and formal question.
verses.before: So Pilate came outside to them and asked, “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”
verses.after: So Pilate came outside to them and asked, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Pilate went out to them and said, “What accusation do you bring against this man?”

verses.rationale: Keeps conditional claim and handover.
verses.before: They answered, “If he were not doing evil, we would not have handed him over to you.”
verses.after: They answered him, “If this man were not doing evil, we would not have handed him over to you.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They answered him, “If this man were not doing evil, we would not have handed him over to you.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Pilate’s directive, their law, and stated restriction.
verses.before: Pilate said, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your Law.” The Jewish leaders said, “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death.”
verses.after: Pilate told them, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law.” The Judean leaders replied, “We are not permitted to put anyone to death.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law.” The Judeans said to him, “It is not lawful for us to put anyone to death.”

verses.rationale: Keeps fulfillment and the manner-of-death explanation.
verses.before: This happened so that Jesus’ word might be fulfilled, indicating what kind of death he was about to die.
verses.after: This happened so that Jesus’ word would be fulfilled, indicating what kind of death he was about to die.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was to fulfill the word that Jesus had spoken to show by what kind of death he was going to die.

verses.rationale: Preserves movement, summons, title, and question.
verses.before: Pilate went back into the headquarters, called Jesus, and asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?”
verses.after: Pilate went back into the headquarters, summoned Jesus, and asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Pilate entered the headquarters again and called Jesus and said to him, “Are you the King of the Judeans?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the two possible sources of Pilate’s question.
verses.before: Jesus answered, “Are you saying this from yourself, or did others tell you about me?”
verses.after: Jesus answered, “Are you saying this on your own, or did others tell you about me?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered, “Do you say this from yourself, or did others say it to you about me?”

verses.rationale: Preserves Pilate’s distancing question, agents of handover, and demand.
verses.before: Pilate answered, “I am not a Jew, am I? Your own nation and chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”
verses.after: Pilate replied, “I am not Jewish, am I? Your own nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pilate answered, “Am I a Judean? Your own nation and the chief priests have handed you over to me. What have you done?”

verses.rationale: Preserves origin rather than location of kingdom, counterfactual fighting, handover, and repetition.
verses.before: Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom were from this world, my servants would fight so that I would not be handed over to the Jewish leaders. But now my kingdom is not from here.”
verses.after: Jesus answered, “My kingdom does not come from this world. If my kingdom came from this world, my servants would be fighting to keep me from being handed over to the Judean leaders. But as it is, my kingdom does not come from here.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered, “My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom were from this world, my servants would be fighting so that I might not be handed over to the Judeans. But as it is, my kingdom is not from here.”

verses.rationale: Keeps disputed royal formulation, birth, coming, witness, truth, belonging, and voice.
verses.before: Pilate said, “So you are a king?” Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to testify to the truth. Everyone who is from the truth listens to my voice.”
verses.after: Pilate asked him, “So you are a king?” Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pilate said to him, “So you are a king?” Jesus answered, “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I have come into the world: to bear witness to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth listens to my voice.”

verses.rationale: Preserves question, movement, audience, and acquittal statement.
verses.before: Pilate asked him, “What is truth?” After saying this, Pilate went out again to the Jewish leaders and said, “I find no basis for a charge against him.
verses.after: Pilate asked him, “What is truth?” After saying this, he went outside again to the Judean leaders and told them, “I find no basis for a charge against him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pilate said to him, “What is truth?” After saying this, he went out again to the Judeans and told them, “I find no case against him.

verses.rationale: Keeps custom, one prisoner, festival, and provocative title.
verses.before: But you have a custom that I release someone for you at Passover. Do you want me to release for you the king of the Jews?”
verses.after: But you have a custom that I release one prisoner to you at Passover. So do you want me to release the king of the Jews?”
verses.tsw_comparator: But you have a custom that I release one prisoner for you at Passover. So do you want me to release for you the King of the Judeans?”

verses.rationale: Preserves crowd choice and renders the term’s range beyond a mere private thief.
verses.before: They shouted back, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a robber.
verses.after: They shouted again, “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a violent rebel.
verses.tsw_comparator: They cried out again, “Not this one, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a bandit.

verses.rationale: Preserves Pilate’s authority and brutal punishment.
verses.before: Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.
verses.after: Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pilate took Jesus and had him flogged.

verses.rationale: Keeps soldiers’ actions and mocking royal objects.
verses.before: The soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns, put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple robe.
verses.after: The soldiers wove a crown from thorns, put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple robe.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns and placed it on his head, and they clothed him in a purple robe.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated mockery and physical abuse.
verses.before: They kept coming up to him and saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!” and slapping him.
verses.after: They kept coming up to him and saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!” And they slapped him.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came up to him again and again, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!” and they struck him with their hands.

verses.rationale: Keeps movement, public presentation, purpose, and repeated acquittal.
verses.before: Pilate went outside again and said to them, “Look, I am bringing him out to you so that you may know I find no basis for a charge against him.”
verses.after: Pilate went outside again and told them, “Look, I am bringing him out to you so that you may know I find no basis for a charge against him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Pilate went out again and said to them, “Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may know that I find no case against him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves clothing, movement, and Pilate’s terse presentation.
verses.before: Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and purple robe. Pilate said to them, “Look—the man!”
verses.after: Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. Pilate told them, “Here is the man!”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. Pilate said to them, “Behold, the man.”

verses.rationale: Keeps agents, repeated demand, Pilate’s reply, and acquittal.
verses.before: When the chief priests and officers saw him, they shouted, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate said, “Take him yourselves and crucify him, because I find no basis for a charge against him.”
verses.after: When the chief priests and officers saw him, they shouted, “Crucify him! Crucify him!” Pilate told them, “Take him and crucify him yourselves, because I find no basis for a charge against him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the chief priests and the officers saw him, they cried out, “Crucify! Crucify!” Pilate said to them, “Take him yourselves and crucify him; for I find no case against him.”

verses.rationale: Preserves law, death claim, and stated charge.
verses.before: The Jewish leaders answered, “We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die because he made himself God’s Son.”
verses.after: The Judean leaders answered him, “We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die because he made himself the Son of God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The Jews answered him, “We have a law, and according to that law he ought to die, because he has made himself the Son of God.”

verses.rationale: Keeps cause and increased fear.
verses.before: When Pilate heard this statement, he became even more afraid.
verses.after: When Pilate heard this statement, he became even more afraid.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Pilate heard this statement, he was even more afraid.

verses.rationale: Preserves movement, origin question, and silence.
verses.before: He went back into the headquarters and asked Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.
verses.after: He went back into the headquarters and asked Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.
verses.tsw_comparator: He entered the headquarters again and said to Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.

verses.rationale: Keeps Pilate’s affront and twin claims of authority.
verses.before: Pilate said, “You will not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to release you and authority to crucify you?”
verses.after: So Pilate asked him, “You will not speak to me? Don’t you know that I have authority to release you and authority to crucify you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So Pilate said to him, “You refuse to speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to release you, and authority to crucify you?”

verses.rationale: Preserves derivative authority, above ambiguity, causal conclusion, handover, and comparative guilt.
verses.before: Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has greater sin.”
verses.after: Jesus answered him, “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given to you from above. Therefore, the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus answered him, “You would have no authority over me unless it had been given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Pilate’s effort, political threat, friendship title, and opposition claim.
verses.before: From then on Pilate tried to release him, but the Jewish leaders shouted, “If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. Everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.”
verses.after: From then on Pilate kept trying to release him, but the Judean leaders shouted, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.”
verses.tsw_comparator: From then on Pilate tried to release him, but the Jews cried out, “If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.”

verses.rationale: Preserves response, movement, judicial seat, and both place names.
verses.before: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judge’s seat at a place called Stone Pavement, and in Hebrew Gabbatha.
verses.after: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, or in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judge’s seat at a place called The Stone Pavement, or in Hebrew, Gabbatha.

verses.rationale: Keeps festival timing, approximate sixth hour, audience, and title.
verses.before: It was the day of Preparation for Passover, about the sixth hour. Pilate said to the Jewish leaders, “Look—your king!”
verses.after: It was the day of preparation for Passover, about noon. Pilate told the Judean leaders, “Here is your king!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now it was the day of Preparation for the Passover, and it was about noon. He said to the Jews, “Here is your king.”

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated rejection, crucifixion demand, Pilate’s question, and chief priests’ declaration.
verses.before: They shouted, “Take him away! Take him away! Crucify him!” Pilate asked, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.”
verses.after: They shouted, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate asked them, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They cried out, “Away with him! Away with him! Crucify him!” Pilate said to them, “Shall I crucify your king?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king but Caesar.”

verses.rationale: Keeps judicial handover, purpose, and custody transfer.
verses.before: Then Pilate handed Jesus over to them to be crucified.
verses.after: Then Pilate handed Jesus over to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he handed him over to them to be crucified.

verses.rationale: Preserves Jesus’ carrying, movement, and translated place names.
verses.before: and carrying the cross by himself, he went out to the place called Place of the Skull, which is called Golgotha in Hebrew.
verses.after: Carrying the cross himself, he went out to the place called Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
verses.tsw_comparator: So they took Jesus, and he went out, bearing the cross himself, to the place called The Place of the Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.

verses.rationale: Keeps location, execution, exact number, and arrangement.
verses.before: There they crucified him, and with him two others, one on each side, with Jesus between them.
verses.after: There they crucified him, along with two others, one on each side and Jesus in the middle.
verses.tsw_comparator: There they crucified him, and with him two others, one on either side, with Jesus between them.

verses.rationale: Preserves writer, placement, and full inscription.
verses.before: Pilate also wrote a notice and put it on the cross. It read, “Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews.”
verses.after: Pilate also wrote a notice and placed it on the cross. It read: Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews.
verses.tsw_comparator: Pilate also had an inscription written and placed on the cross. It read, “Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews.”

verses.rationale: Keeps broad readership, geographic reason, and three languages.
verses.before: Many Jewish people read this notice because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
verses.after: Many Jewish people read this notice because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city. It was written in Hebrew, Latin, and Greek.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many of the Jews read this inscription, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city, and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.

verses.rationale: Preserves the leaders’ requested distinction between title and reported claim.

verses.rationale: Keeps beloved disciple’s recognition, Peter’s clothing action and state, and plunge.
verses.before: The disciple Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!” When Simon Peter heard it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment, because he was stripped for work, and threw himself into the sea.
verses.after: The disciple Jesus loved told Peter, “It is the Lord!” When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he tied his outer garment around himself, because he was stripped for work, and plunged into the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord.” When Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he put on his outer garment (for he was stripped for work) and threw himself into the sea.

verses.rationale: Preserves boat size, net, fish, proximity, and ancient approximate measure.
verses.before: The other disciples came in the little boat, dragging the net full of fish, because they were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits away.
verses.after: The other disciples came in the small boat, dragging the net full of fish, because they were not far from land—only about two hundred cubits.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the other disciples came in the little boat, for they were not far from the land, but about two hundred cubits, dragging the net full of fish.

verses.rationale: Keeps landing, charcoal fire, fish, and bread.
verses.before: When they came ashore, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish lying on it and bread.
verses.after: When they came ashore, they saw a charcoal fire there with fish lying on it, and bread.
verses.tsw_comparator: So when they had come onto the land, they saw a charcoal fire laid there, and fish placed on it, and bread.

verses.rationale: Preserves command and fresh catch.
verses.before: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you just caught.”
verses.after: Jesus told them, “Bring some of the fish you just caught.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus said to them, “Bring some of the fish that you have just caught.”

verses.rationale: Keeps Peter’s actions, exact number, size, abundance, and intact net.
verses.before: Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net ashore, full of large fish—one hundred fifty-three of them. Even though there were so many, the net was not torn.
verses.after: So Simon Peter climbed aboard and hauled the net ashore, full of 153 large fish. Even with so many, the net was not torn.
verses.tsw_comparator: Simon Peter went up and drew the net to land, full of large fish—one hundred fifty-three; and though there were so many, the net was not torn.

verses.rationale: Preserves invitation, reluctance, unasked question, and recognition.
verses.before: Jesus said, “Come and have breakfast.” None of the disciples dared ask him, “Who are you?” because they knew it was the Lord.
verses.after: Jesus told them, “Come and eat breakfast.” None of the disciples dared ask him, “Who are you?” because they knew it was the Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus said to them, “Come, eat breakfast.” None of the disciples dared to ask him, “Who are you?” knowing that it was the Lord.

verses.rationale: Keeps Jesus’ actions and parallel distribution.
verses.before: Jesus came, took the bread, and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish.
verses.after: Jesus came, took the bread, and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and likewise the fish.

verses.rationale: Preserves counted appearance and resurrection setting.
verses.before: This was now the third time Jesus was revealed to the disciples after being raised from the dead.
verses.after: This was now the third time Jesus appeared to the disciples after he had been raised from the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: This was now the third time Jesus was revealed to the disciples after he was raised from the dead.

verses.rationale: Keeps full address, ambiguous comparison, exchanged love verbs without overstating their distinction, knowledge, and commission.
verses.before: When they had eaten breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?” Peter said, “Yes, Lord. You know that I love you.” Jesus told him, “Feed my lambs.”
verses.after: After they had eaten breakfast, Jesus asked Simon Peter, “Simon son of John, do you love me more than these?” He answered, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” Jesus told him, “Feed my lambs.”
verses.tsw_comparator: So when they had eaten breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of John, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.”

verses.rationale: Preserves second count, love, knowledge, and shepherding command.
verses.before: He asked him a second time, “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Peter said, “Yes, Lord. You know that I love you.” Jesus told him, “Shepherd my sheep.”
verses.after: Jesus asked him a second time, “Simon son of John, do you love me?” He answered, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” Jesus told him, “Shepherd my sheep.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him again a second time, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I love you.” He said to him, “Shepherd my sheep.”

verses.rationale: Keeps third count, grief, repeated question, comprehensive knowledge, and commission.
verses.before: He asked him the third time, “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Peter was grieved because Jesus asked him the third time, “Do you love me?” He said, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I love you.” Jesus told him, “Feed my sheep.”
verses.after: Jesus asked him a third time, “Simon son of John, do you love me?” Peter was grieved that Jesus asked him the third time, “Do you love me?” He answered, “Lord, you know everything; you know that I love you.” Jesus told him, “Feed my sheep.
verses.tsw_comparator: He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of John, do you love me?” Peter was grieved because he said to him the third time, “Do you love me?” And he said to him, “Lord, you know all things; you know that I love you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.

verses.rationale: Preserves double amen, age contrast, dressing, freedom, outstretched hands, and compelled movement.
verses.before: “Truly, truly, I tell you, when you were younger, you tied your own belt and walked where you wanted. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will tie you and carry you where you do not want to go.”
verses.after: Truly, truly, I tell you: when you were younger, you dressed yourself and walked wherever you wanted. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and someone else will dress you and carry you where you do not want to go.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Truly, truly, I say to you, when you were younger, you used to dress yourself and walk where you wished. But when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you and carry you where you do not wish.”

verses.rationale: Keeps narrator’s death interpretation, glory, and direct command.
verses.before: He said this to indicate by what kind of death Peter would glorify God. After saying this, he told him, “Follow me.”
verses.after: Jesus said this to indicate the kind of death by which Peter would glorify God. After saying this, he told him, “Follow me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now he said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. And after saying this he said to him, “Follow me.”

verses.rationale: Preserves turn, beloved disciple, following, meal identification, and earlier question.
verses.before: Peter turned and saw the disciple Jesus loved following them—the one who had leaned back against Jesus at the supper and asked, “Lord, who is the one handing you over?”
verses.after: Peter turned and saw the disciple Jesus loved following them—the one who had leaned back against Jesus at the supper and asked, “Lord, who is going to betray you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Peter, turning around, saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following—who also had leaned back against Jesus at the supper and said, “Lord, who is it who is betraying you?”

verses.rationale: Keeps Peter’s sight and comparative question.
verses.before: When Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”
verses.after: When Peter saw him, he asked Jesus, “Lord, what about this man?”
verses.tsw_comparator: So when Peter saw him, he said to Jesus, “Lord, and what about this man?”

verses.rationale: Preserves hypothetical condition, coming, refusal of comparison, and emphatic command.
verses.before: Jesus said, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”
verses.after: Jesus told him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jesus said to him, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps community, rumor, correction, and exact conditional saying.
verses.before: So this saying spread among the brothers that this disciple would not die. But Jesus did not tell Peter that he would not die; he said, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”
verses.after: So this saying spread among the brothers and sisters that this disciple would not die. But Jesus did not tell Peter that he would not die; he said, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore this saying went out among the brothers that that disciple would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but, “If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?”

verses.rationale: Preserves witness, authorship claim, communal knowledge, and truth.
verses.before: This is the disciple who testifies about these things and wrote these things, and we know that his testimony is true.
verses.after: This is the disciple who testifies about these things and wrote them down, and we know that his testimony is true.
verses.tsw_comparator: This is the disciple who testifies about these things, and who wrote these things; and we know that his testimony is true.

verses.rationale: Keeps expansive hyperbole, first-person judgment, world, and books.
verses.before: There are also many other things Jesus did. If every one of them were written down, I suppose the world itself could not contain the books that would be written.
verses.after: There are also many other things Jesus did. If every one were written down, I suppose the world itself could not contain the books that would be written.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there are also many other things that Jesus did, which if they were written one by one, I suppose that even the world itself would not have room for the books that would be written.
